title: Two Weird New Sea Spiders Found — One Has Hairy Feet and Red Eyes!
summary:
Imagine tiny hairy legs creeping up your body while you swim at night. That's what one newly discovered sea spider looks like! Scientists at the University of British Columbia found two brand-new sea spider species in the Salish Sea. It's the first time anyone has described new sea spiders there in almost 100 years.

Sea spiders are NOT normal spiders. They are ancient cousins of spiders and scorpions that have lived in the ocean for about 500 million years. Some have up to 12 legs! They breathe through their skin, and the dads carry the eggs.

One new species is called Callipallene pilosuspedes. That name means "hairy feet" in Latin. It has long, curved spines on its legs, bright red eyes, and a mouth shaped like a triangle with three lips. Scientists say it looks like a tiny monster from a movie.

Here's the weird part: they only found ONE of these spiders. Just one!

The second species is named Tanystylum kiixin (say "kee-hin"). It's named after an old Indigenous village site, and the name sounds like waves crashing on the shore.

Why does this matter? Scientists need to know what animals live in the ocean so they can protect them as the climate changes.
why_it_matters: The ocean is home to millions of animals we still don't know about, and the more we discover, the better we can take care of ocean life for the future.

background_read: The Salish Sea (the ocean water between the Canadian city of Vancouver and the U.S. state of Washington) is full of life, including orcas, salmon and giant octopuses.
The University of British Columbia (a large research university in Canada) is where the scientists who found these sea spiders work.
Sea spiders are an ancient family of ocean animals — they were already living in the sea hundreds of millions of years before dinosaurs appeared.
Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists at the University of British Columbia, who described two new sea spider species.
WHAT: They found Callipallene pilosuspedes, a hairy-legged, red-eyed spider-like animal, and Tanystylum kiixin, named after an old Indigenous village site.
WHERE: In the Salish Sea — the first new sea spiders described there in almost 100 years.
WHY: Knowing which animals live in the ocean helps scientists protect them as the climate changes.

perspectives.description: Researchers are thrilled because finding a brand-new species — especially one that looks like a tiny movie monster — shows how much of the ocean is still a mystery.
Some people point out that the ocean is changing because of warming and pollution, so naming new species quickly matters if we want to save them.
Others say that finding only ONE of these spiders means we can't yet tell whether the species is common or very rare.
